Join Diagnostics

Source: R/diagnostics.R
sv_join_diagnostics.Rd

Checks a join before you run it: how many rows match in each direction, the key relationship (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many), how many rows each join type returns, missing and duplicated keys, a sample of unmatched keys, and fixes that would match more rows, each measured on its own (trimming whitespace, ignoring case, dropping leading zeros). Keys are compared the way dplyr joins compare them by default, so NA matches NA.

Usage

sv_join_diagnostics(x, y, by, sample_n = 5L, x_name = "x", y_name = "y")

Arguments

x, y

Data frames to join (x is the left table).

by

Join columns: a character vector as in dplyr::left_join(), where names are columns of x and values columns of y (c("id", "site" = "site_code")). Unnamed entries use the same name on both sides.

sample_n

Number of unmatched keys to list for each side.

x_name, y_name

Table names used in messages.

Value

An object of class sv_join_diagnostics: a list with by (data frame of x/y columns), n_x, n_y, distinct_x, distinct_y, distinct_matched, matched_x, matched_y (rows with a partner), match_rate_x, match_rate_y, na_x, na_y (rows with a missing key), dup_keys_x, dup_keys_y (keys that occur more than once), relationship, rows (named list of row counts per join type), unmatched_x, unmatched_y (sample keys), type_issues, hints (list of fix, label, extra_x, extra_y), warnings and status ("ok", "warn" or "error").

Details

The canvas runs this whenever two columns are connected and shows the result on the join step and in the Discrepancy tab.

Examples

patients <- data.frame(id = c(1, 2, 3, 4), age = c(40, 51, 62, 33))
visits <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2, 5), visit = 1:4)
sv_join_diagnostics(patients, visits, by = "id")
#> <sv_join_diagnostics> by id
#>   relationship: one-to-many
#>   x rows matched: 2 of 4 (50.0%)
#>   y rows matched: 3 of 4 (75.0%)
#>   rows after join: left 5 | inner 3 | full 6 | right 4 | semi 2 | anti 2 
#>   unmatched in x: 3; 4 
#>   unmatched in y: 5
